learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Understands the basic mechanisms of heat transport in steady-state and transient situations and applies the appropriate analytical calculation tools.
Fluently handles simple computer tools for calculating heat transfer with numerical methods in transient and steady-state and evaluates their results.
Understands common heat production procedures, analyzes the behavior of corresponding equipment, and applies appropriate calculation tools for creating simple calculation models.

syllabus_topics: 2 - Fundamentals of heat conduction: Fourier's law, EDC
teaching_methods: Lectures: Sessions with the professor where the syllabus will be explained and practical examples will be given
Problem and case solving: Practical sessions where problems related to theoretical concepts are solved
Simulation and laboratory practices: Computer simulation exercises, accompanied by experimental data collection in some cases, of thermal systems
Personal study and work: Preparation for classes, completion of exercises, etc.
assessment_rules: There will be a single global evaluation procedure. Practical activities will account for 20% of the grade. A written exam will account for 80% of the final grade, requiring a minimum of 4.5/10 to pass the course. The practical activities grade is retained for the enrollment period; otherwise, related questions may be included in the written exam for up to 20% of the total value.
